newsitem.title: USA: Fed needs price target timetable - Ex-Fed's Hoskins.
newsitem.headline: Fed needs price target timetable - Ex-Fed's Hoskins.

text.p: The Federal Reserve should adopt a timetable as well as an inflation target to make price stability a credible policy goal, a former Fed bank president said.
"You can't just say, 'We want price stability and that's the goal of the Fed,'" former Cleveland Fed President Lee Hoskins told Reuters in an interview.
"You have to have a time commitment, like a multi-year target over which to achieve it," Hoskins added.

Hoskins, chairman and chief executive officer of Columbus-based Huntington National Bank, was among the first Fed officials to advocate targeting inflation as a means of attaining the central bank's main policy goal of price stability.

"There should be a single objective for the Federal Reserve," said Hoskins. "It should be overridding and nothing else should get in the way; that's the quest toward zero inflation and we consistently talked about that since February of 1988."
Hoskins said targeting the Consumer Price Index (CPI) has the advantage of clearly conveying policy goals to the public.
"The public does not know about price stability but they do know about the CPI," noted Hoskins, adding that the notion has been debated within the Fed since 1988.

"It was a way to market the idea of price level stability and we pursued that both as an educational effort with the public and policy makers, as well as a real goal for the Federal Reserve," Hoskins added.
Hoskins called the issue of whether the CPI overstates inflation a "red herring."
"If there is a bias, and you know what it is, then, fix the index," the former Cleveland Fed president stated.
Hoskins also believes the Fed should be held accountable for its ability to attain and maintain steady price levels.

"You have to have a penalty. New Zealand has a penalty," said Hoskins, referring to New Zealand's system in which the central bank governor may be replaced if monetary policy fails to maintain inflation within an announced target.
"You don't achieve it, you get fired," Hoskins added.
The Fed's current dual mandate calls for the central bank to seek maximum employment and fight inflation.
Hoskins supports the idea of giving a single anti-inflation mandate.
However, Hoskins also said a pending bill in Congress to that effect "has no teeth" because it does not include a timeframe for the Fed to achieve its goal.
Hoskins said credible legislation would include a timetable within which inflation should be wiped out, so that "on average, over a two- or three-year period, you have to achieve price stability."
Hoskins is also vice chairman and CEO of Huntington National's parent company, Huntington Bancshares Inc.
